claims.text: The WTaTiVZr alloy is equimolar, corresponding nominally to 20 at.% each of W, Ta, Ti, V, and Zr.
The as-cast WTaTiVZr HEA has an initially coarse microstructure.
The initial microstructure of the as-cast HEA is comparable to that of commercially pure tungsten.
Cyclic mechanical loading at approximately 1200°C can trigger dynamic recrystallization in the WTaTiVZr HEA.
A moderate strain-rate regime exists that promotes dynamic recrystallization without causing complete or destructive grain coarsening.
Cyclic high-temperature loading produces fine, dynamically recrystallized grains in the HEA.
The dynamically recrystallized grains in the HEA undergo cyclical renewal during loading.
Transient high-angle grain boundaries form in the HEA during cyclic high-temperature loading.
Pure tungsten retains a relatively static and coarser grain structure under the same loading conditions.
Dynamic recrystallization dissipates localized stress in the HEA.
Dynamic recrystallization minimizes dislocation pile-ups in the HEA.
Renewal of the refined grain structure delays crack initiation and propagation in the HEA.
The proposed dynamic-recrystallization mechanism increases the HEA's toughness.
The proposed dynamic-recrystallization mechanism increases the HEA's plastic strain relative to pure tungsten.
The HEA will exhibit cycle-dependent grain refinement detectable by time-resolved EBSD.
The HEA will retain a finer and more consistent grain structure throughout cyclic loading than pure tungsten.
The HEA will have greater cycle life than pure tungsten under identical cyclic loading at approximately 1200°C.
The HEA will have higher strain-to-failure than pure tungsten under identical cyclic loading at approximately 1200°C.
Crack formation will occur later in the HEA than in pure tungsten.
The proposed mechanism applies within typical plasma-facing-component service timescales.
